title: A New Tax System (Medicare Levy Surcharge—Fringe Benefits) Amendment (Excess Levels for Private Health Insurance Policies) Bill 2018
short_title: A New Tax System (Medicare Levy Surcharge—Fringe Benefits) Amendment (Excess Levels for Private Health Insurance Policies) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a three-bill package that implements private health insurance reforms from October 2017.

It amends the Private Health Insurance Act 2007 to give insurers more flexibility, including age-based discounts and higher voluntary excess levels, and expands the Private Health Insurance Ombudsman's powers.
The package also allows insurers to cover travel and accommodation for regional Australians and lets them terminate products and transfer policyholders to new ones.
changes: Allow age-based premium discounts for hospital cover.
Increase maximum voluntary excess levels for products exempting individuals from the Medicare levy surcharge.
Strengthen the Private Health Insurance Ombudsman's inspection and audit powers.
Permit insurers to cover regional Australians' travel and accommodation as part of hospital treatment.
Allow insurers to terminate products and transfer affected policyholders to new products.
Remove benefit limitation periods to improve consumer transparency.
summary.affected: Private health insurers, policyholders, and the Private Health Insurance Ombudsman.

speeches.speaker: Greg Hunt
speeches.brief: The government introduced a package of private health insurance reforms, including discounts of up to 10% for Australians under 30 on hospital cover, a premium increase of 3.95% from 1 April 2018 (the lowest in 17 years), and measures to strengthen the Ombudsman's powers, allow insurers to cover travel and accommodation costs, and improve consumer transparency.

speeches.speaker: Greg Hunt
speeches.brief: The Medicare Levy Amendment (Excess Levels for Private Health Insurance Policies) Bill 2018 increases maximum excess amounts for private hospital cover to $750 for singles and $1,500 for couples and families, allowing insurers to offer lower premiums. The bill also removes grandfathering provisions that exempted certain pre-2007 policies from the Medicare levy surcharge.

speeches.speaker: Greg Hunt
speeches.brief: The speaker announced a package of private health insurance reforms including increased maximum excess levels (the first increase since 2001), age-based premium discounts for young Australians, strengthened powers for the Private Health Insurance Ombudsman, coverage of travel and accommodation for rural patients, a simplified consumer statement, and removal of benefit limitation periods, along with two tax bills to maintain Medicare levy surcharge exemptions.
